rows.label: Share of Dogs Trust's 2025 international spending that went on rabies control (dog vaccination, rabies education and surveillance)

source.title: Dogs Trust Annual Report 2025 (year to 31 December 2025): consolidated SOFA, notes 1 and 7(a)

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both of charityevals' Dogs Trust models so the split is one number: the rabies model's cost is this share of the £26.1m international line, the dog-welfare model's the rest. The accounts don't split international work by activity. Anchor: Worldwide Veterinary Service (WVS, consolidated) spent £11.8m (note 1), which vaccinated 2.2 million dogs at about $2.18 to $3.45 a dose where WVS pays the whole cost (Gibson et al. 2022, Goa), though governments supply vaccine and vaccinators in several of its campaigns, so roughly £3.5m to £5m of WVS's spending; grants outside the group to rabies programmes (BSPCA Malawi £1.08m, PDAFF Cambodia £0.09m, Guinea's livestock ministry £0.26m, Bangladesh's health directorate £0.23m, Timor-Leste's vets £0.14m, part of Soi Dog's and Hope & Animal Trust's, note 7(a)) add about £2m. Together about £6.5m of £26.1m, 25%; 15% to 40% because WVS's cost split isn't published. The rest is Dogs Trust Ireland and Bosnia (rehoming, neutering), WVS's treatment, sterilisation and training, and the other overseas grants.
